newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fyffes expects a successful 1997.
newsitem.headline: Fyffes expects a successful 1997.

text.p: Fruit distribution group Fyffes Plc said on Monday that it expected 1997 to be another successful year for the company.

"While Fyffes has expanded substantially over the past three years, its strong cash flow and good operating profits provide an excellent base for continued progress," the company said in its annual results statement.

Fyffes, which has operations in eight European countries, reported a 15 percent increase in profit before tax and goodwill to 48.5 million Irish pounds, while operating profit was up 23 percent at 47.1 million.

"The underlying strength of our business, our broad spread of fresh produce, the wide range of geographic markets in which we operate and the success of our recent acquisitions together have enabled us to produce a record result for 1996," chairman Neil McCann said.
"We believe that 1997 will be another successful year for Fyffes," he added.
McCann said Fyffes had obtained attractive returns from a number of sizable acquisitions and capital expenditures in 1996.
Acquisitions accounted for 94 percent of a total 20 percent increase in sales, the company said.
In Ireland and Britain, sales were up by 18 percent to 732 million Irish pounds while sales in continental Europe rose by 23 percent to 666 million.
Overall operating profit rose by 23 percent but Fyffes said profits from the group's continuing operations declined slightly.

"The overall increase derives from the operating profits generated from acquisitions and associated undertakings," Fyffes said. The group's operating margin rose to 3.3 percent from 3.2 percent a year earlier.

A geographic breakdown showed Ireland and Britain accounted for 28 million Irish pounds of operating profits, a rise of 15 percent while profits in continental Europe were up 36 percent at 20 million.
Losses in the U.S. market were similar to the previous year at one million Irish pounds and Fyffes' business in the U.S. has now been terminated, the company said.
Last January, Fyffes and its joint venture partner, The Windward Island Banana Development and Export Co, acquired the banana business of Geest Plc for 147.5 million stg.
Fyffes said its share of the consolidated pre-tax profit of the joint venture before a goodwill charge but after deducting interest costs was 5.3 million Irish pounds.
It said it was happy with progress on restructuring the Geest business and integrating other recent acquisitions.
The group remains on the lookout for companies to buy.

At October 31, 1996, Fyffes had shareholders' funds of 200 million Irish pounds and net cash of 70 million, giving it the capacity to take advantage of attractive opportunities, McCann said. He said the group would in particular look for acquisitions in continental Europe.
